govdocs-archive_org-TheFinalNailInMalach: The Last Nail in Malachi Martin’s box — a web sheaf — goes after the runaway Jesuit’s good name. The file fits the hot church-row shelf. Martin’s friends answer its charges. The row splits the old-Mass folk. Both sides claim the papers. Read it with both eyes open.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-BelliMelvin_Bel: This item — Belli, Melvin — is a National Security Internet Archive file. The file’s full context is unclear. Melvin Belli was the flamboyant San Francisco lawyer. Its subject seems to be the JFK case. Archivists value such fragments. The item is a fragment of the archive.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-BrownHRapBombin: This Newsweek piece — Terrorism on the Left — covers left-wing political violence. The 1970s saw bombings and kidnappings. The Weather Underground made headlines. The era was violent. The file belongs to the political archive. The item is a fragment of press history.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-DiesMartin_Dies: Martin Dies’s Martin Dies’ Story is the congressman’s memoir. The file belongs to the political archive. Dies chaired the House Un-American Activities Committee. His red-hunting shaped an era. The memoir defends his record. The item is a fragment of political history.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-DymondFIrwin_Dy: This item — Dymond, F. Irwin — is a National Security Internet Archive file. The file’s full context is unclear. F. Irwin Dymond defended Clay Shaw. Shaw was acquitted in 1969. The trial was a sensation. The item is a fragment of the archive.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-FBINewOrleansFi: This FBI memorandum — HSCA Request for Field Office Assassination Files — is a Bureau file. The declassified memo is a primary source. The committee wanted the field files. Researchers value such files. The file belongs to the assassination archive.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-InternationalTr: This I.E. Zollinger Co. appraisers/auctioneers photo listing ad is a trade item. Auctioneers appraised the era’s goods. The ad is a curiosity. Ephemera tells its own story. The file belongs to the business archive. The item is a fragment of commercial history.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-KingMartinLuthe: This investigation of the assassination of Martin Luther King — House Select Committee on Assassinations — is a probe file. The committee reopened the King case. The file belongs to the government archive. The item is a fragment of the record.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-PostalInspector: These postal inspector notes — New Orleans, November 22, 1963, creator unknown — are a mail file. Inspectors tracked the mail trails. The notes may hold a clue. The file belongs to the government archive. The item is a fragment of the record.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-Pre-Assassinati: This letter to Frank — November 16, 1942, creator unknown — is a wartime note. Wartime letters carry the era’s weight. The note may hold a clue. The file belongs to the personal archive. The item is a fragment of correspondence.
greifenstein: F. Marion Crawford sets this dramatic novel among the German aristocracy, in the shadow of the ancient castle of Greifenstein. Pride, family honor, and a tragic secret drive the von Greifenstein family toward a shattering reckoning. Crawford's cosmopolitan storytelling — he wrote of half the countries of Europe — gives the tale both grandeur and intimate feeling.
facts-and-arguments-for-darwin: German naturalist Fritz Müller, working in Brazil, wrote this early and powerful defense of Darwin's theory of evolution. From his studies of crustaceans he drew evidence that species change over time, sending the book to Darwin himself — who called it invaluable. A key document from the years when evolution was still fighting for acceptance.
mark-twain: Archibald Henderson knew Mark Twain himself, and his life of the humorist draws on that friendship. From Hannibal boyhood to world fame — river pilot, miner, newsman, and beloved sage — Twain's story unfolds warmly. An early and most trustworthy portrait of a great American.
annals-and-reminiscences-of-jamaica-plai: Harriet Manning Whitcomb gathers the annals of Jamaica Plain — the Boston suburb's old houses, families, and changing ways. Local history lovingly told. A treasure for all who love New England's past. Old families, vanished customs, and the growth of a Boston suburb live again in her affectionate pages.
erema-or-my-father-s-sin: R. D. Blackmore's heroine Erema bears the shadow of her father's sin in this tale of love and atonement. Set against wild Exmoor, it shows the Lorna Doone author's power in a gentler key. A moving romance of guilt and grace.
william-tell-told-again: Wodehouse retells William Tell for children — the apple, the tyrant Gessler, and Swiss freedom — with his own comic spin. Even legends get the Wodehouse treatment. A merry introduction to the great tale. Gessler's hat, the apple shot, and freedom's fight get the comic treatment.
the-bravest-of-the-brave-or-with-peterbo: Henty's hero serves with Peterborough in Spain during the War of the Spanish Succession — sieges, battles, and daring exploits. The bravest of the brave live up to their name. Stirring historical adventure. Almanza's field and Barcelona's siege test his hero's mettle to the full.
a-brief-history-of-panics-and-their-peri: Clément Juglar's brief history of panics traces America's financial crashes and their rhythm. His pioneering work founded the study of business cycles. Economics history of lasting value. His Juglar cycles still figure in every economics textbook. Boom and bust march through his pages in fateful rhythm.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-abbey-of-lehn: The Encyclopedia's Lehnin entry: the Cistercian house of Brandenburg's sands. Grey monks tamed the wilderness. Richard Urban Butler writes its story. Prayer in the pine woods. The prophecy of Lehnin made its name famous in legend. Its brick church stands among the pines.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-abthain: This 1913 reference piece on the abthain — the old Scottish church office, half abbot, half steward. Thomas Walsh explains its Celtic roots. Land and prayer met in the title. A relic of the early Scottish Church. Its lands passed to lay lords at last.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-adele-amalie-: This 1913 reference piece on Princess Gallitzin — Adele Amalie, the German convert of Münster. Patricius Schlager tells her story. Her salon became a Catholic circle. Goethe mourned her going to Rome. A soul that found its home. Her son became a missionary in America.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-akhmin: This 1913 reference piece on Akhmin — the old Egyptian city of the Copts. Henri Leclercq notes its Christian past. Martyrs bled in its pagan temples. The Nile guards its ancient stones. A Pharaonic town turned Christian. Its papyri enrich the world's museums.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-albert-jean-b: This 1913 reference article on Albert Belin — a French churchman of letters. Alexius Hoffmann notes his works. The entry preserves his modest fame. A writer in the Church's service. His books served the faithful. His sermons edified the faithful. His diocese mourned a devoted shepherd.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-albrecht-von-: A 1913 entry on Wallenstein — the imperial general of the Thirty Years' War. Martin Spahn tells his meteoric tale. His armies were states on the march. Eger's assassins ended his dreams. The warlord of the German tragedy. His palace in Prague keeps his memory.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-alcuin: A 1913 entry on Alcuin — Charlemagne's scholar, England's gift to Europe. James Burns honors his school at Tours. He taught the palace and the realm. His letters charmed an age. The father of the Carolingian renaissance. His textbooks taught the medieval schools.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-altar-curtain: A 1913 entry on altar curtains — the riddel curtains at the altar's sides. Augustin Schulte traces their old use. They veiled the mysteries in Lent. Their folds framed the sacred action. The altar's modest drapery. Their rings still hang in old churches.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-andre-garin: This 1913 reference piece on André Garin — the Oblate missionary of British Columbia. Adrian Morice honors his labors. He served the Indian missions for decades. The far west knew his zeal. A pioneer priest of the Pacific. His chapel stands in the Cariboo.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-anne-therese-: A 1913 entry on Mother Théodore Guérin — the foundress of Saint Mary-of-the-Woods. Alma Le Brun honors her Indiana mission. She crossed the sea for souls. The wilderness tested her faith. The frontier's saintly mother. Her schoolhouse rose in the forest.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-artvin: This 1913 reference article on Artvin — a town of the Armenian highlands. Joseph Lins notes its modest record. The entry preserves its scanty fame. The missions remember their stations. A station of the eastern missions. Its valleys hid the Armenian villages.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-ascelin: A 1913 Catholic Encyclopedia entry on Ascelin — the Dominican envoy to the Tartars. Thomas Schwertner tells his bold journey. He carried the pope's letters to the Khan. The Mongol court heard his preaching. A friar at the world's edge. His report reached the Paris chroniclers.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-august-allers: This 1913 reference piece on August Allerstein — a Jesuit of the China mission. Thomas Campbell records his career. The entry preserves his modest fame. The Society honors its distant laborers. A missionary of the Celestial Empire. His maps charted the Chinese provinces.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-augustus-welb: This 1913 reference piece on Augustus Pugin — the prophet of the Gothic revival. Henry Parkinson honors his churches. His designs rebuilt Catholic England. The convert's zeal fired his pencil. The architect of the new Middle Ages. His Contrasts preached the Gothic gospel.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-baldwin: This 1913 reference article on Baldwin — a name in the crusading story. Michael Ott records what is known. The entry preserves his modest fame. The chronicles of Outremer keep his name. A figure of the Latin East. His deeds live in the chronicles.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-bassein: This 1913 reference piece on Bassein — a diocese of the eastern missions. Peter Fernandez gives its story. Its bishops serve the coastal flock. The entry traces its mission past. A see of the tropical shore. Its churches face the tropical sea.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-benin: A 1913 entry on Benin — the West African missions. Albert Battandier tells its hard story. The priests braved the fever coast. The missions' foothold was dearly won. The Church's Gulf of Guinea frontier. Its bronzes are the museums' pride.
